concepts.title: Human Development and Family Studies as a Discipline

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Human Development and Family Studies as a Discipline' refers to.
questions.a: HDFS studies the changes people undergo from birth to old age and trains professionals to serve persons of different ages, needs and circumstances, treating home and workplace with equal respect.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Human Development and Family Studies as a Discipline'.
questions.a: Colleges rename the field Child Development, Human Development and Childhood Studies or Human Ecology, differing in emphasis but not in substance.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Human Development and Family Studies as a Discipline', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: qualitative idea -- one discipline serving the whole life span

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Attachment and Recognition in Infancy' refers to.
questions.a: Babies bind themselves to the mother and other close carers, show fear of unknown faces around eight to twelve months, cry when the caregiver leaves and trail after her -- behaviour that fades as the toddler grasps that an absent mother has not vanished.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Attachment and Recognition in Infancy'.
questions.a: Stranger fear is a milestone, not a mischief: it proves the baby can tell familiar from unfamiliar faces.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Attachment and Recognition in Infancy', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: sequence -- recognition to attachment to separation protest to security

concepts.title: Substitute Care: Creche and Day Care

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Substitute Care: Creche and Day Care' refers to.
questions.a: When the mother works outside, another woman of the household, a neighbourhood home creche or an institutional centre can stand in; a creche formally designates an institution built for infants and young children away from home care, while day care covers preschoolers as well.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Substitute Care: Creche and Day Care'.
questions.a: Substitute care frees an older sibling for school and brings nutrition and health inputs to disadvantaged children.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Substitute Care: Creche and Day Care', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: care ladder -- family member to home creche to institutional centre

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Objectives of ECCE' refers to.
questions.a: Early childhood care and education aims at the all round development of the child so full potential unfolds, readies the child for school, and stands behind women and children as a support service.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Objectives of ECCE'.
questions.a: Preschool complements, never replaces, the learning that happens naturally at home.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Objectives of ECCE', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: three aims -- holistic development plus school readiness plus support to women and children

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Guiding Principles of ECCE' refers to.
questions.a: ECCE practice rests on play as the engine of learning, art as the base of education, respect for the special texture of children's thinking, lived experience over rote expertise, a mix of formal and informal exchanges, local materials and cultures, developmentally apt flexibility, and attention to health and well being.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Guiding Principles of ECCE'.
questions.a: Routines should mix the familiar with gentle challenge, so curiosity survives and anxiety stays away.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Guiding Principles of ECCE', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: principle set -- play plus art plus experience plus locality plus flexibility plus health

concepts.title: Age Stages: Infancy, Toddler, Preschool Child

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Age Stages: Infancy, Toddler, Preschool Child' refers to.
questions.a: Early childhood stretches from birth to eight years, split at three; infancy covers the first year or two of total dependence; the two to three year old is a toddler whose walk still jumps; and the preschool child, ready for company beyond the family, may attend a Montessori school or an anganwadi under ICDS.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Age Stages: Infancy, Toddler, Preschool Child'.
questions.a: Different stages need differently trained adults: infant care and preschool teaching are distinct skill sets.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Age Stages: Infancy, Toddler, Preschool Child', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: stage bands -- infancy to 1 or 2 years, toddler 2 to 3, preschool 3 to 6, early childhood to 8

concepts.title: Child Centred Approach and the Play Way Method

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Child Centred Approach and the Play Way Method' refers to.
questions.a: A good preschool runs on the child centred, play way route: learning arrives through enjoyable activity among peers, the setting stays safe, loving and rich in people and play material, and no child is forced into desk bound lessons that wither curiosity.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Child Centred Approach and the Play Way Method'.
questions.a: Children eat by themselves and try new foods among peers; the right setting teaches what nagging cannot.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Child Centred Approach and the Play Way Method', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: method -- enjoyment plus peers plus caring adult plus play material, without formal drill

concepts.title: Piaget and Vygotsky for the ECCE Teacher

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Piaget and Vygotsky for the ECCE Teacher' refers to.
questions.a: Piaget showed that young children understand the world in ways of their own and must explore at their own pace, while Vygotsky stressed how much a concerned, knowledgeable adult matters; together they set the teacher's task -- know what the child can do and pitch every activity neither too easy nor too hard.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Piaget and Vygotsky for the ECCE Teacher'.
questions.a: The preschool educator must know the child's capabilities more than facts about the world.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Piaget and Vygotsky for the ECCE Teacher', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: task difficulty -- below interest threshold plus above frustration threshold, both avoided

concepts.title: Skills and Training for ECCE Professionals

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Skills and Training for ECCE Professionals' refers to.
questions.a: An early childhood worker needs genuine interest in children, knowledge of their needs and capacities, stamina for long physical activity, a repertoire of stories, songs and art skills, flexibility to drop a lesson plan mid stream, plus administrative ability for records and parent contact; entry runs through nursery teacher training, one year diplomas or a degree with child development and psychology.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Skills and Training for ECCE Professionals'.
questions.a: Short attention spans make a large stock of ready activities and quick adaptability compulsory.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Skills and Training for ECCE Professionals', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: profile -- interest plus knowledge plus arts repertoire plus stamina plus flexibility plus administration

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Scope and Careers in ECCE' refers to.
questions.a: Trained workers serve as nursery teachers, creche and day care caregivers, programme team members, campaign planners in government and NGOs, teacher trainers or entrepreneurs running camps, activity clubs and preschool centres, and can climb to postgraduate and doctoral study.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Scope and Careers in ECCE'.
questions.a: Entrepreneurship means setting up one's own programme at home or in separate space, which adds management expertise to teaching skill.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Scope and Careers in ECCE', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: service map -- creches plus day care plus nursery schools plus NGOs plus ICDS plus training institutes

questions.q: Calculate the width in years of a stage that begins at birth and ends at age one. Use the method 'Span of Developmental Stages'. Work with: end_age = 10, start_age = 10. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of stage_span.
questions.a: 0 years

questions.q: Find the number of years between the start and end ages of any stated developmental band. Use the method 'Span of Developmental Stages'. Work with: end_age = 1000, start_age = 150. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of stage_span.
questions.a: 850 years

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Span of Developmental Stages' refers to.
questions.a: Each developmental stage occupies a stated age band, and the width of any band in years is the upper age minus the lower age of that band.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Span of Developmental Stages'.
questions.a: The toddler band covers one year, infancy one to two, and the preschool band four years from three to seven.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Span of Developmental Stages', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: stage_span = end_age - start_age

questions.q: Compute the share of the birth to 8 window taken up by the first year of life. Use the method 'Infancy Share of Early Childhood'. Work with: childhood_end = 100, childhood_start = 6, infancy_years = 100. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of infancy_pct.
questions.a: 106.383 per cent

questions.q: Find what fraction in per cent one stage forms of the whole birth to eight window. Use the method 'Infancy Share of Early Childhood'. Work with: childhood_end = 240, childhood_start = 15, infancy_years = 500. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of infancy_pct.
questions.a: 222.2222 per cent

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Infancy Share of Early Childhood' refers to.
questions.a: Since early childhood runs from birth to eight years, the one year of infancy occupies a fixed percentage of that window, found by dividing the infancy span by the whole span and scaling to one hundred.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Infancy Share of Early Childhood'.
questions.a: One year out of eight makes infancy one eighth, about 12.5 per cent, of early childhood.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Infancy Share of Early Childhood', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: infancy_pct = infancy_years / (childhood_end - childhood_start) * 100
